reason: Moses (Mosheh) is a regular person character who appears prominently throughout this passage with multiple qualities: (1) Direct speech lines - he speaks to God several times, e.g., 'וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אָסֻֽרָה־ נָּ֣א וְאֶרְאֶ֔ה' ('And Moses said, I will now turn aside and see'); (2) Explicit emotions - he expresses fear: 'כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔א מֵהַבִּ֖יט אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִֽים' ('for he was afraid to look upon God'); (3) Opinions and concerns - he questions his adequacy for the mission: 'מִ֣י אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אֵלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה' ('Who am I that I should go unto Pharaoh').
